Bob Dylan and Keith Richards on stage at Live Aid, JFK Stadium, Philadelphia, July 13, 1985.

It was not the smoothest set of the day. The stage was busy getting ready for the finale behind them and the three of them had trouble hearing each other. At one point Dylan broke a string and Ronnie Wood handed over his own guitar and kept going on air guitar until a roadie brought another.

Dylan also said, on stage, that he hoped some of the money could go to American farmers who were losing their land. Those words helped start Farm Aid, which held its first concert that September.

Love it or not, it is one of the most talked about moments of the whole day, and the picture says a lot. Keith with his arm in the air, Bob in the middle of it all.

Every month for six years, someone has posted exactly £5 through my letterbox.

My name is Frances, I'm seventy four, and the envelopes started the week after my husband died. No name, no return address, just a plain brown envelope and a crisp five pound note, always landing on the mat on the first of the month.

I never spent a single one. I kept them in a biscuit tin on top of the wardrobe, and I'd counted seventy two of them. £360.

This month I decided enough was enough. On the last night of the month I pulled a chair up to the front door, wrapped myself in a blanket and stayed awake with a flask of tea.

At six in the morning, I heard the gate creak. A shadow fell across the glass, and the letterbox flap lifted just slightly. I threw the door open before the envelope could drop.
